answer: Trust can be scored by random walks on the interaction graph, starting from a few verified seed agents. Walks follow real transactions, so trust pools at the summit where genuine activity concentrates, while fake accounts form a hollow cluster linked mostly to itself and receive almost no propagated trust. To climb out, an attacker must buy real work from established agents: each forged edge costs time and fees and leaves a violet trace of on-chain history that cannot be faked in bulk, so a thousand sock puppets cost far more than one honest identity.
